# Border

A border is a width token paired with a color token.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Border.mdx`

## Overview

Borders mark a boundary, separate neighbors and show state. The width token sets how heavy the line is and the color token says what it means, so always choose them as a pair.

```css
border-width: var(--border-width-default);
border-width: var(--border-width-selected);
border-width: var(--border-width-focused);
```

Figma holds `Border/default`, `Border/selected` and `Border/focused` in `spacing / semantics`, paired with `color/border/*` in `color / semantics`.

## Width tokens

Three widths cover every border. Pick by what the line says, never by how heavy you want it to look. Values are indicative; the tokens are the contract.

- `--border-width-default` (Border/default): Every standard border and divider: field edges, table lines, section rules.
- `--border-width-selected` (Border/selected): The chosen option in a group: an active tab, a selected tile or row.
- `--border-width-focused` (Border/focused): The focus ring that shows keyboard users where they are.

## Pair width with color

Take both width and color from this table.

| Width | Color | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/default` | Edges and dividers that only separate. |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/input` | A field’s outline. |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/danger` | An invalid field. |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/disabled` | A disabled control. |
| `Border/selected` | `color/border/selected` | The selected option in a group. |
| `Border/focused` | `color/border/focused` | The focus ring. Use `color/border/focused/inverse` on a dark surface. |

## Focus ring

The focus ring shows keyboard users where they are. It is a ring, never a fill: a filled field looks selected or disabled.

| Fact | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Width | 2 px, `--border-width-focused` |
| Distance | 2 px away from the control (`--focus-ring-width`) |
| Color | `color/border/focused` (`--ds-border-focused`); `color/border/focused/inverse` on a dark surface |
| Radius | The control’s radius plus 2 px. Radius owns the pairs. |
| Containers | Cards and modals draw no ring of their own |

## Selected states

A selected option, active tab or chosen tile takes `Border/selected` (2 px) in `color/border/selected` on every side, paired with a second cue such as a check or a fill. State and emphasis use the whole shape, never a colored stripe on one edge.

## Dividers

- Space comes first. Add a 1 px line (`Border/default` in `color/border/default`) only when spacing alone does not separate two groups.
- A horizontal rule spans the content width of its container. A vertical rule sits between controls and takes their height.
- A heavier or colored line is a state, not a divider.

## Borders in patterns

Take pattern borders from this table rather than adding one of your own.

| Pattern | Line | Token | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Table | Grid lines and the head rule | `color/border/default` · `color/border/bold` | The selected row fills the whole row with color/background/selected. The checkbox is the second cue. |
| Docked sidebar | One 1 px divider on the edge that faces the Page | `color/border/default` | The topbar and the Page carry no border of their own. |
| Banner | None | — | Meaning comes from the fill and the icon. |
| Card | None | — | The edge comes from elevation, not a border. |

### Give the sidebar one edge and the topbar none

The sidebar ends in a 1 px divider in `color/border/default`. The topbar has no border.

## Do and don't

### Show selection with the whole outline

A selected row takes the 2 px selected border on every side, in `color/border/selected`.

### Use the selected width only for selection

`Border/default` is the width for everything that is not a state.

## Accessibility

- A border that is the only cue for a control's edge clears 3:1 against its surround (WCAG 1.4.11). Use `color/border/input` for fields.
- The focus ring is the one signal for keyboard focus and clears 3:1 against what it sits on.
- Selection never rests on color alone: the 2 px width is the second cue beside `color/border/selected`.
- A subtle accent background needs an accent border to reach 3:1 against the surface.
